rules.title: Ban on coordinated pricing algorithms for rents
rules.requirement: It is illegal to sell rent-setting algorithms that use private competitor data to Berkeley landlords, and illegal for landlords to use them to set rents or occupancy levels. Each month and each unit is a separate violation.
rules.requirement_es: Es ilegal vender a los propietarios de Berkeley algoritmos que usan datos privados de competidores para fijar rentas, y es ilegal que los propietarios los usen para fijar rentas o niveles de ocupación. Cada mes y cada unidad cuenta como una violación separada.
rules.key_value: Up to $1,000 civil penalty per violation
rules.coverage_text: Residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley. Covers any process using nonpublic competitor data (less than 90 days old) to recommend rents, fees, occupancy or lease terms; excludes aggregated anonymous reports, affordable-housing rent/income limit tools, and market research, appraisal, or software development uses.

source.title: D001
source.quote:
B. It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm described 
in subsection A when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in 
the City of Berkeley.

rules.title: Tenant screening fee rights statement required
rules.requirement: If a Berkeley landlord charges a screening or application fee, they must give you, before taking the fee, a written statement of your screening fee rights and the maximum fee allowed by state law.
rules.requirement_es: Si un arrendador en Berkeley cobra una tarifa de evaluación o de solicitud, debe darle, antes de recibir la tarifa, una declaración escrita de sus derechos sobre la tarifa de evaluación y el monto máximo permitido por la ley estatal.
rules.coverage_text: Owners or agents in Berkeley who charge a fee to purchase a consumer credit report and process a rental application.

source.title: D005
source.quote: When an owner or the owner’s agent gets a request to rent residential property in Berkeley from an applicant and the owner charges a fee to purchase a consumer credit report and to validate, review, or otherwise process an application, the owner must provide, either in the rental application or in a separate disclosure before receiving the fee, a clear and conspicuous tenant screening fee rights statement and a statement of the maximum fee cap permitted under

rules.title: No non-refundable fees to renew a tenancy or change roommates
rules.requirement: A Berkeley landlord cannot charge a current tenant a non-refundable fee to renew a tenancy, including fees when a roommate leaves or when you ask to add or replace a roommate.
rules.requirement_es: Un arrendador en Berkeley no puede cobrar a un inquilino actual una tarifa no reembolsable para renovar el arrendamiento, incluidas las tarifas cuando un compañero de casa se va o cuando usted pide agregar o reemplazar a un compañero.
rules.coverage_text: Existing tenants of residential rental property in Berkeley; applies regardless of contrary lease language.

source.title: D005
source.quote: An owner of residential rental property (or the owner’s agent) cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy, in whole or in part, including any fee associated with the departure of a roommate or to request to add or replace a roommate in a pre-existing household.

rules.title: Relocation assistance for Ellis Act evictions
rules.requirement: If a landlord evicts you to take the property off the rental market (Ellis Act), the landlord must pay you the same relocation money as for an owner move-in eviction. Starting January 1, 2026, that is $19,413, plus $6,471 more for qualifying households.
rules.requirement_es: Si el propietario lo desaloja para retirar la propiedad del mercado de alquiler (Ley Ellis), debe pagarle la misma ayuda de reubicación que en un desalojo para ocupación del propietario. Desde el 1 de enero de 2026, son $19,413, más $6,471 adicionales para hogares que califiquen.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants evicted so the owner can remove the property from the rental housing market under Berkeley's Ellis Implementation Ordinance.

source.title: D004
source.quote: The Ellis Implementation Ordinance requires the same relocation assistance payments for tenants evicted so the owner can remove a property from the rental housing market.

rules.title: Just cause eviction (Measure BB changes)
rules.requirement: Tenants in fully or partially covered Berkeley units can only be evicted for a just cause. A tenant cannot be evicted for unpaid rent of less than one month's Fair Market Rent, or for refusing to sign a similar new lease.
rules.requirement_es: Los inquilinos de unidades de Berkeley con cobertura total o parcial solo pueden ser desalojados por una causa justa. No se puede desalojar a un inquilino por renta impaga menor a un mes de la Renta Justa de Mercado, ni por negarse a firmar un nuevo contrato similar.
rules.key_value: nonpayment eviction requires debt of at least one month's Fair Market Rent
rules.coverage_text: Units fully or partially covered by the Berkeley Rent Ordinance. Eviction notices must refer tenants to the Rent Board, and copies must be filed with the Rent Board within three business days of service.

source.title: D006
source.quote: In Berkeley, tenants in units that are fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance cannot be evicted unless there is "just cause” (previously called “good cause”).

rules.title: Relocation assistance for owner move-in evictions
rules.requirement: If a landlord evicts you so the owner can move in, the landlord must pay you relocation money. Starting January 1, 2026, the standard payment is $19,413, plus $6,471 more for qualifying households.
rules.requirement_es: Si el propietario lo desaloja para mudarse a la unidad, debe pagarle una ayuda de reubicación. Desde el 1 de enero de 2026, el pago estándar es de $19,413, más $6,471 adicionales para hogares que califiquen.
rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance
rules.coverage_text: Tenants evicted for owner move-in under Berkeley's Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance.

source.title: D004
source.quote: The Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance requires owners to pay tenants relocation assistance in the event of an owner move-in eviction.

rules.title: Berkeley 2026 Annual General Adjustment (1.0%)
rules.requirement: For 2026, eligible Berkeley landlords may raise rent ceilings on covered units by no more than 1.0%, starting no earlier than January 1, 2026. The yearly increase is set at 65% of the Bay Area inflation rate (CPI).
rules.requirement_es: Para 2026, los propietarios elegibles de Berkeley pueden aumentar los topes de renta de las unidades cubiertas en no más de 1.0%, a partir del 1 de enero de 2026 como muy pronto. El aumento anual se fija en el 65% de la inflación (IPC) del Área de la Bahía.
rules.coverage_text: Eligible landlords of units with permanent rent ceilings under the Berkeley Rent Ordinance; conditions for qualifying are in Rent Board Regulation 1148.

source.title: D008
source.quote:
At its regular meeting on October 16, 2025, the Berkeley Rent Stabilization Board 
adopted the Annual General Adjustment (AGA) Order for Year 2026 which will allow 
eligible landlords to increase the 2025 permanent rent ceilings by 1.0% no earlier than 
January 1, 2026.

rules.title: Annual General Adjustment capped at 5% (Measure BB)
rules.requirement: In fully covered Berkeley units, rent can rise each year only by the Annual General Adjustment set by the Rent Board, which is tied to inflation and can be no more than 5%.
rules.requirement_es: En las unidades de Berkeley con cobertura total, la renta solo puede subir cada año según el Ajuste General Anual que fija la Junta de Renta, ligado a la inflación y que no puede ser mayor del 5%.
rules.coverage_text: Fully covered units (rent ceiling): most units in multifamily properties built before 1980, single-family homes with tenancies that began before 1996, and single-family homes with five or more rooms rented separately. Partially covered (no rent ceiling): new construction with a certificate of occupancy issued after 1980, most single-family homes, and most condominiums. Government-owned or subsidized units are now fully or partially covered depending on unit type. Landlords with banked AGAs from prior years may still raise rent above 5% up to the rent ceiling.

source.title: D006
source.quote: The maximum AGA is 5%.

rules.title: Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance (criminal history)
rules.requirement: Landlords in Berkeley may not ask about or use criminal history or criminal background checks in ads, applications, tenant selection, or decisions. If a landlord acts based on criminal history where allowed, they must give written notice and a chance to respond.
rules.requirement_es: Los arrendadores en Berkeley no pueden preguntar ni usar antecedentes penales ni verificaciones de antecedentes penales en anuncios, solicitudes, selección de inquilinos o decisiones. Si un arrendador actúa por antecedentes penales cuando está permitido, debe dar aviso por escrito y la oportunidad de responder.
rules.coverage_text: Applies to rental housing providers in Berkeley for current and prospective tenants. Exemptions (see ordinance for details): lifetime sex offenders; limited exemptions for public housing/Section 8; owner-occupied properties of 1-3 units where an owner of record lives in one unit; units rented under an agreement letting owners move back (BMC 13.76.130 A.9); existing tenants subletting or adding/replacing roommates.

source.title: D003
source.quote: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.

rules.title: Berkeley security deposit interest
rules.requirement: In Berkeley units fully or partly covered by the Rent Ordinance, landlords must pay tenants interest on their security deposit every year, plus a prorated amount if the tenant moves out before year end.
rules.requirement_es: En las unidades de Berkeley cubiertas total o parcialmente por la Ordenanza de Renta, los propietarios deben pagar a los inquilinos intereses sobre su depósito de seguridad cada año, más una cantidad prorrateada si el inquilino se muda antes de fin de año.
rules.coverage_text: Tenancies in units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance.

source.title: D007
source.quote: For tenancies in units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance, landlords must pay tenants interest on their security deposit at the end of each year and a prorated amount if the tenant moves out before the end of the year.

rules.title: RSO no-fault eviction relocation assistance
rules.requirement: For no-fault evictions from rent-stabilized (RSO) units in Los Angeles, the landlord must file a Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD and pay relocation assistance within 15 days of the notice. For July 2026 to June 2027 the amounts range from $11,000 to $27,400 depending on tenancy length, income, and whether the tenant is qualified (62+, disabled, or with minor children).
rules.requirement_es: En desalojos sin culpa de unidades con renta estabilizada (RSO) en Los Ángeles, el propietario debe presentar una Declaración de Intención de Desalojo ante LAHD y pagar asistencia de reubicación dentro de 15 días del aviso. De julio de 2026 a junio de 2027 los montos van de $11,000 a $27,400 según la duración del arrendamiento, los ingresos y si el inquilino es calificado (62+ años, con discapacidad o con hijos menores).
rules.coverage_text: No-fault evictions (owner/relative/manager occupancy, demolition or removal from rental use, government order to vacate, conversions, etc.) from units covered by the Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance. Reduced amounts for Mom and Pop properties for owner/family occupancy evictions.

source.title: D043
source.quote:
All tenant not- at-fault evictions require payment of relocation assistance and the filing of a 
Declaration of Intent to Evict form with the Los Angeles Housing Department (LAHD) before 
evicting tenants from units covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or the Just Cause 
Ordinance (JCO).

rules.title: JCO no-fault eviction relocation assistance
rules.requirement: For no-fault evictions from units covered by the Just Cause Ordinance (JCO) in Los Angeles, the landlord must file a Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD and pay relocation assistance within 15 days of the notice. Amounts range from $11,000 to $27,400 for July 2026 to June 2027, or one month's rent for certain single-family homes owned by individuals.
rules.requirement_es: En desalojos sin culpa de unidades cubiertas por la Ordenanza de Causa Justa (JCO) en Los Ángeles, el propietario debe presentar una Declaración de Intención de Desalojo ante LAHD y pagar asistencia de reubicación dentro de 15 días del aviso. Los montos van de $11,000 a $27,400 de julio de 2026 a junio de 2027, o un mes de renta para ciertas casas unifamiliares de personas físicas.
rules.key_value: $11,000–$27,400 per unit (July 1, 2026–June 30, 2027); one month's rent for single-family homes owned by natural persons
rules.coverage_text: No-fault evictions from units covered by the Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance. Single-family dwellings owned by a natural person who owns no more than four units and a single-family home in the City pay one month's rent.

source.title: D043
source.quote:
All tenant not- at-fault evictions require payment of relocation assistance and the filing of a 
Declaration of Intent to Evict form with the Los Angeles Housing Department (LAHD) before 
evicting tenants from units covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or the Just Cause 
Ordinance (JCO).

rules.title: Resident Protections Ordinance relocation for demolition
rules.requirement: If a Los Angeles landlord demolishes a protected unit to build new housing, lower-income tenants must get enhanced relocation payments (for 2026-27, up to $115,480 under the standard option), and all tenants get at least the RSO or JCO amount.
rules.requirement_es: Si un propietario en Los Ángeles demuele una unidad protegida para construir nueva vivienda, los inquilinos de bajos ingresos deben recibir pagos de reubicación mayores (para 2026-27, hasta $115,480 bajo la opción estándar), y todos los inquilinos reciben al menos el monto de RSO o JCO.
rules.coverage_text: Protected Units demolished for new construction within 5 years after filing the Notice of Intent to Withdraw or Declaration of Intent to Evict; Protected Units include all RSO units and units with recent affordability covenants, rent control, lower-income occupants, or Ellis Act withdrawal.

source.title: D043
source.quote:
Owners who demolish a Protected Unit for the purpose of new construction within 5 years after the 
filing of the Notice of Intent to Withdraw or Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD are required to 
comply with relocation requirements under the RPO.

rules.title: Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance (JCO)
rules.requirement: In Los Angeles, most rental units not under rent control can only be ended for a legal reason listed in the law. If you are evicted for a no-fault reason, like the owner moving in, your landlord may have to pay you relocation money.
rules.requirement_es: En Los Ángeles, la mayoría de las unidades que no están bajo control de renta solo pueden terminarse por una razón legal de la lista de la ley. Si lo desalojan sin culpa suya, por ejemplo porque el dueño se muda, el propietario puede tener que pagarle dinero de reubicación.
rules.coverage_text: Most residential properties in the City of Los Angeles not regulated by the RSO, including single-family dwellings, once the tenant has lived in the unit 6 months or the original lease has expired, whichever comes first. Exceptions include transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity/sorority houses, owner's roommate, certain cooperatives, some non-profit homeless or substance-abuse facilities, and some HACLA or government-owned properties. Since March 27, 2023, tenants cannot be evicted for nonpayment unless they owe more than the Fair Market Rent for the unit size.

source.title: D040
source.quote: It prohibits terminations of tenancies without just cause and requires relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.

rules.title: RSO annual allowable rent increase (July 2025 - June 2026)
rules.requirement: For units covered by the Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance, the yearly rent increase from July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026 is limited to 3%. Starting February 2, 2026, landlords can no longer add an extra percentage for utilities.
rules.requirement_es: Para las unidades cubiertas por la Ordenanza de Estabilización de Rentas de Los Ángeles, el aumento anual de renta del 1 de julio de 2025 al 30 de junio de 2026 está limitado al 3%. A partir del 2 de febrero de 2026, los arrendadores ya no pueden agregar un porcentaje adicional por servicios públicos.
rules.citation: City of Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO)
rules.coverage_text: Rental units subject to the City of Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO).

source.title: D042
source.quote:
Annual rent increases for rental units subject to the City of Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO), effective
July 1, 2025, through June 30, 2026
is
3%

rules.title: Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) annual increase limit
rules.requirement: For rent-stabilized units, rent may go up only once every 12 months, by the allowable percentage set each year. When a tenant moves out voluntarily or is evicted for certain reasons, the rent can be reset to market rate.
rules.requirement_es: En las unidades con renta estabilizada, la renta solo puede subir una vez cada 12 meses, según el porcentaje permitido que se fija cada año. Cuando un inquilino se muda voluntariamente o es desalojado por ciertas razones, la renta puede ajustarse al precio de mercado.
rules.key_value: allowable annual percentage, once every 12 months
rules.coverage_text: Generally applies to rental properties in the City of Los Angeles first built on or before October 1, 1978 (plus replacement units under LAMC 151.28): apartments, condos and townhomes, duplexes, two or more single-family dwellings on one parcel, long-stay hotel/rooming house units, units attached to commercial buildings, ADUs/JADUs, and mobile homes. Rent amount is not regulated for condo/townhome tenancies that began after December 31, 1995.

source.title: D041
source.quote: Rent may be increased once every 12 months by the allowable rent increase percentage

rules.title: Proposed ban on anti-competitive automated rent price-fixing
rules.requirement: This proposed ordinance would make it illegal to sell or license rent-setting software that uses private competitor data, and illegal for landlords to use it to set rents or occupancy levels. Tenants could sue for up to $1,000 per violation.
rules.requirement_es: Esta ordenanza propuesta haría ilegal vender o licenciar software para fijar rentas que use datos privados de competidores, e ilegal que los arrendadores lo usen para fijar rentas o niveles de ocupación. Los inquilinos podrían demandar hasta $1,000 por cada infracción.
rules.coverage_text: Persons selling, licensing or providing algorithmic devices that use nonpublic competitor data, and landlords of residential rental property in the City of San Diego. Excludes software publishing reports from public or 90+ day-old aggregated data, and software used for affordable housing program rent/income limits.

source.title: D076
source.quote:
It is unlawful for a landlord to use an algorithmic device to set rental rates
or occupancy levels for residential rental property.

rules.title: San Diego Residential Tenant Protections (just cause and relocation)
rules.requirement: Your landlord cannot end your tenancy without a just cause listed in the law, such as unpaid rent or the owner moving in. For no-fault evictions, the landlord must pay relocation help equal to two months' rent (three months if you are a senior or disabled), either in cash or by waiving rent.
rules.requirement_es: Su propietario no puede terminar su arrendamiento sin una causa justa indicada en la ley, como renta no pagada o que el dueño se mude a la vivienda. En desalojos sin culpa, el propietario debe pagar ayuda de reubicación igual a dos meses de renta (tres meses si usted es una persona mayor o tiene una discapacidad), en efectivo o eximiendo la renta.
rules.key_value: Relocation: 2 months' rent (3 months for seniors or disabled tenants)
rules.citation: San Diego Mun. Code ch. 9, art. 8, div. 7
rules.coverage_text: Residential rental property in the City of San Diego, including mobilehome park units, with a tenancy of more than 30 days, unless exempt.

source.title: D073
source.quote:
A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause. For purposes of this 
Division, just cause includes at-fault just cause and no-fault just cause.

rules.jurisdiction: City and County of San Francisco
rules.title: Ban on algorithmic devices to set rents
rules.requirement: Landlords in San Francisco may not use, and companies may not sell, software that analyzes private competitor rent data to recommend rents or manage occupancy. Tenants or the City Attorney can sue over violations.
rules.requirement_es: En San Francisco, los propietarios no pueden usar, y las empresas no pueden vender, programas que analizan datos privados de alquiler de competidores para recomendar rentas o manejar la ocupación. Los inquilinos o el Abogado de la Ciudad pueden demandar por violaciones.
rules.coverage_text: Residential units in San Francisco; covers any device such as software that uses algorithms to analyze nonpublic competitor rental data to recommend rent for a vacant unit.

source.title: D081
source.quote:
Legislation
adding Section 37.10C to the Rent Ordinance went into effect on October 14, 2024. The law prohibits the sale or use of algorithmic devices to set rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units in San Francisco.

rules.requirement: If you are evicted in San Francisco for an owner or relative move-in, demolition or removal of the unit, capital improvement work, or substantial rehab, your landlord must pay you $8,245 per tenant (up to $24,733 per unit), plus $5,497 more for each elderly (60+) or disabled tenant or household with minor children, for notices served 3/1/2026-2/28/2027.
rules.requirement_es: Si lo desalojan en San Francisco porque el dueño o un familiar se muda, por demolición o retiro de la unidad, por obras de mejora de capital o por rehabilitación sustancial, el propietario debe pagarle $8,245 por inquilino (hasta $24,733 por unidad), más $5,497 por cada inquilino mayor (60+) o discapacitado u hogar con hijos menores, para avisos entregados del 1/3/2026 al 28/2/2027.
rules.key_value: $8,245 per tenant; max $24,733 per unit; +$5,497 per elderly/disabled tenant or household with minor children (for eviction notices served 3/1/2026-2/28/2027)
rules.coverage_text: Evictions in San Francisco based on owner/relative move-in, demolition/permanent removal from housing use, temporary capital improvement work (20 days or more), or substantial rehabilitation; amounts based on date the eviction notice is served.

rules.jurisdiction: City and County of San Francisco
rules.title: Just cause required for evictions
rules.requirement: In units covered by the San Francisco Rent Ordinance, a landlord can only evict you for one of 17 listed just-cause reasons. The lease simply ending or a change in owner is not a just cause.
rules.requirement_es: En unidades cubiertas por la Ordenanza de Alquiler de San Francisco, el propietario solo puede desalojarlo por una de 17 causas justas enumeradas. El simple vencimiento del contrato o un cambio de dueño no es causa justa.
rules.coverage_text: Rental units covered by the Rent Ordinance, including newer units (certificate of occupancy after June 13, 1979) and Costa-Hawkins units that are exempt from rent increase limits.

source.title: D079
source.quote: In order to evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing the eviction.

rules.jurisdiction: City and County of San Francisco
rules.title: San Francisco annual allowable rent increase (3/1/2026-2/28/2027)
rules.requirement: For rent-controlled units in San Francisco, the most your landlord can raise your rent for the yearly increase from March 1, 2026 to February 28, 2027 is 1.6%.
rules.requirement_es: Para unidades con control de renta en San Francisco, lo máximo que el propietario puede subir la renta en el aumento anual del 1 de marzo de 2026 al 28 de febrero de 2027 es 1.6%.
rules.citation: San Francisco Rent Board, Annual Rent Increase for 3/1/26 - 2/28/27
rules.coverage_text: Rent-controlled units in San Francisco.

source.title: D080
source.quote: For rent-controlled units, the annual allowable increase amount effective March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 1.6%.

rules.title: Santa Ana just cause eviction
rules.requirement: After 30 days of tenancy, a Santa Ana landlord must have a just cause listed in the law and state it in a written notice to end your tenancy. For no-fault evictions, the landlord must pay 3 months of relocation assistance or waive the last 3 months of rent.
rules.requirement_es: Después de 30 días de arrendamiento, el propietario en Santa Ana debe tener una causa justa establecida en la ley e indicarla por escrito para terminar su arrendamiento. En desalojos sin culpa, el propietario debe pagar 3 meses de asistencia de reubicación o perdonar la renta de los últimos 3 meses.
rules.citation: Santa Ana Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.coverage_text: Residential tenancies in Santa Ana after 30 days, except housing produced in the last 15 years, deed-restricted affordable housing, hotel and transient occupancy, hospital and care facilities, dormitories, and other shared living quarters.

source.title: D085
source.quote: After 30 days, an owner shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in a written notice.

rules.title: Santa Ana just cause eviction and relocation assistance
rules.requirement: Your landlord needs a valid reason to evict you, such as not paying rent, breaking the lease, or moving into the unit. For some reasons, the landlord may have to help pay your moving costs.
rules.requirement_es: Su propietario necesita una razón válida para desalojarlo, como no pagar la renta, violar el contrato o mudarse a la unidad. Por algunas razones, el propietario podría tener que ayudar a pagar sus gastos de mudanza.
rules.citation: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.coverage_text: Rental units covered by the Santa Ana Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance.

source.title: D084
source.quote: Your landlord must have a valid reason to evict you.

rules.title: Santa Ana annual rent increase cap
rules.requirement: Your landlord can raise rent only once a year, by no more than 3% or 80% of the change in the Consumer Price Index, whichever is lower. From September 1, 2026 through August 31, 2027, the maximum increase is 2.87%.
rules.requirement_es: Su propietario solo puede aumentar la renta una vez al año, no más del 3% o del 80% del cambio en el Índice de Precios al Consumidor, lo que sea menor. Del 1 de septiembre de 2026 al 31 de agosto de 2027, el aumento máximo es de 2.87%.
rules.citation: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.coverage_text: Rental units covered by the Santa Ana Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance.

source.title: D084
source.quote: The increase cannot be more than 3% of your current rent or 80% of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) change, whichever is less.

rules.title: Santa Ana rent stabilization cap
rules.requirement: In Santa Ana, rent can go up by no more than 3% per year or 80% of the change in CPI, whichever is lower. If CPI is negative, no rent increase is allowed.
rules.requirement_es: En Santa Ana, la renta puede subir como máximo un 3% al año o el 80% del cambio en el IPC, lo que sea menor. Si el IPC es negativo, no se permite ningún aumento.
rules.coverage_text: Residential rental units in Santa Ana, except buildings constructed after February 1, 1995 and mobile home spaces offered for rent after January 1, 1990.

source.title: D085
source.quote: Increase in residential rents are limited to the lower of 3% per year, or 80% of the percent change in the Consumer Price Index over the most recent 12-month period. If the CPI is negative, no rent increase is permitted.

rules.title: Cartwright Act ban on common pricing algorithms
rules.requirement: In California, it is illegal to use or share a common pricing algorithm (software using competitor data to set or recommend prices or terms) as part of an agreement to restrain trade, or to pressure others to adopt its recommended prices or terms.
rules.requirement_es: En California, es ilegal usar o compartir un algoritmo de precios común (programa que usa datos de competidores para fijar o recomendar precios o condiciones) como parte de un acuerdo para restringir el comercio, o presionar a otros a adoptar sus precios o condiciones recomendados.
rules.coverage_text: Any person (not end consumers) using or distributing a common pricing algorithm, meaning any methodology including software used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend, align, stabilize, set or influence a price or commercial term. Adds Bus. & Prof. Code §§ 16729 and 16756.1.

source.title: D022
source.quote: (a) It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter.

rules.title: Application screening fee cap, receipts and refunds
rules.requirement: A landlord can charge an application screening fee only to cover actual costs, and never more than $30 per applicant (adjusted each year for inflation). You must get an itemized receipt, a copy of your credit report, and a refund if no unit is available, your application is not considered, or the fee is not fully used.
rules.requirement_es: El propietario solo puede cobrar una tarifa de evaluación de solicitud para cubrir los costos reales, y nunca más de $30 por solicitante (ajustado cada año por inflación). Debe recibir un recibo detallado, una copia de su informe de crédito y un reembolso si no hay unidad disponible, si su solicitud no se considera o si la tarifa no se usa por completo.
rules.coverage_text: Applicants for residential rental property, including guarantors and cosigners.

source.title: D026
source.quote: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant.

rules.title: Tenant Protection Act just cause for eviction
rules.requirement: After you have lived in your home for 12 months, your landlord can only end your tenancy for a listed just cause, stated in the written notice. For no-fault reasons, the landlord must pay relocation help or waive the last month's rent, equal to one month's rent.
rules.requirement_es: Después de vivir en su vivienda por 12 meses, el arrendador solo puede terminar su arrendamiento por una causa justa de la lista, indicada en el aviso por escrito. Por causas sin culpa del inquilino, el arrendador debe pagar ayuda de reubicación o perdonar la renta del último mes, igual a un mes de renta.
rules.coverage_text: Residential real property in California after tenants have continuously and lawfully occupied it for 12 months (or 24 months for one tenant when adult tenants are added), unless an exemption applies or a qualifying local just cause ordinance applies.

source.title: D023
source.quote: Notwithstanding any other law, after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.

rules.title: Statewide rent increase cap (Tenant Protection Act)
rules.requirement: Your landlord cannot raise your rent more than 5% plus local inflation, or 10%, whichever is lower, in any 12 months. Rent can be raised at most twice in 12 months.
rules.requirement_es: Su propietario no puede subir el alquiler más del 5% más la inflación local, o el 10%, lo que sea menor, en cualquier período de 12 meses. El alquiler solo puede subirse dos veces como máximo en 12 meses.
rules.coverage_text: Residential real property in California, except affordable/subsidized housing, school dormitories, units under stricter local rent control, housing with a certificate of occupancy in the last 15 years (unless a mobilehome), qualifying separately alienable homes of non-corporate owners with notice, owner-occupied duplexes, and mobilehome homeowners. Initial rent on a new tenancy is not limited.

source.title: D024
source.quote: Subject to subdivision (b), an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, of the lowest gross rental rate charged for that dwelling or unit at any time during the 12 months prior to the effective date of the increase.

rules.title: Limits on criminal history screening (FEHA)
rules.requirement: Landlords may check criminal history but cannot consider arrests without conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile records, and cannot ban everyone with a record. A denial must be based on a conviction directly related to being a good tenant.
rules.requirement_es: Los propietarios pueden revisar antecedentes penales, pero no pueden considerar arrestos sin condena, registros sellados o borrados, ni registros juveniles, y no pueden rechazar a todas las personas con antecedentes. Un rechazo debe basarse en una condena directamente relacionada con ser un buen inquilino.
rules.citation: Cal. Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA) - criminal history
rules.coverage_text: Most housing providers and housing-related services in California, including landlords and tenant screening companies.

Housing providers are also prohibited from having “blanket bans” of all people with a criminal history.

rules.title: Source of income discrimination ban (FEHA)
rules.requirement: Landlords cannot refuse to rent to you or treat you differently because of how you pay rent, including Section 8 vouchers or other rental assistance.
rules.requirement_es: Los propietarios no pueden negarse a alquilarle ni tratarlo de manera diferente por la forma en que paga el alquiler, incluidos los vales de la Sección 8 u otra ayuda para el alquiler.
rules.citation: Cal. Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA) - source of income

rules.title: Source-of-income discrimination ban and credit-history alternative

If you have a rent subsidy, the landlord must base income tests on your share of the rent and let you show other proof of ability to pay instead of credit history.
rules.requirement_es: Los propietarios no pueden rechazarlo ni tratarlo de manera diferente por su fuente de ingresos, incluidos los vales de vivienda de la Sección 8 y otros. Si tiene un subsidio de renta, el propietario debe basar los requisitos de ingresos en su parte de la renta y permitirle mostrar otra prueba de capacidad de pago en lugar de su historial de crédito.

rules.title: Security deposit limited to one month's rent
rules.requirement: Starting July 1, 2024, most landlords may charge a security deposit of no more than one month's rent, whether the unit is furnished or not. Small landlords who are individuals (or family trusts or LLCs of individuals) owning no more than two rental properties with four or fewer units total may charge up to two months' rent.

Los pequeños propietarios que son personas (o fideicomisos familiares o LLC de personas) y que poseen no más de dos propiedades de alquiler con cuatro unidades o menos en total pueden cobrar hasta dos meses de renta.
rules.key_value: one month's rent (two months for qualifying small landlords)

source.title: D007

rules.title: Security deposit cap
rules.requirement: A landlord may not ask for a security deposit of more than one month's rent, on top of the first month's rent. Small landlords (natural persons owning no more than two rental properties with no more than four units) may ask for up to two months' rent, but not from service members.
rules.requirement_es: El arrendador no puede pedir un depósito de garantía de más de un mes de renta, además de la renta del primer mes. Los arrendadores pequeños (personas naturales que tienen no más de dos propiedades de alquiler con no más de cuatro unidades) pueden pedir hasta dos meses de renta, pero no a miembros del servicio militar.
rules.key_value: one month's rent (two months for qualifying small landlords)

Landlords who are natural persons (or LLCs whose members are all natural persons) owning no more than two residential rental properties with no more than four units total may collect up to two months' rent, except from service members. Does not apply to security collected or demanded before July 1, 2024. An advance payment of at least six months' rent is allowed for leases of six months or longer.

rules.title: No discrimination based on rental assistance (source of income)

rules.coverage_text: Housing in Cambridge under the Cambridge Fair Housing Ordinance; protected categories include source of income (Section 8 and public benefits). Exemption for 2-family dwellings where the owner lives there.

source.title: D029
source.quote: Under the law, landlords, sellers and rental agents may use any reasonable standard to determine which applicants are selected, as long as that standard is applied equally and uniformly to all applicants.

rules.requirement: Massachusetts cities and towns may not enact or enforce rent control. A city that accepts this law may only adopt voluntary rent control that cannot regulate evictions, cannot cover owners of fewer than ten units or units with fair market rent above $400, and must compensate owners from city funds.
rules.requirement_es: Las ciudades y pueblos de Massachusetts no pueden adoptar ni aplicar el control de rentas. Una ciudad que acepte esta ley solo puede adoptar un control de rentas voluntario que no puede regular los desalojos, no puede cubrir a dueños de menos de diez unidades ni unidades con renta de mercado mayor de $400, y debe compensar a los dueños con fondos municipales.

rules.requirement: Landlords in Massachusetts may not discriminate against a renter because the renter receives public assistance or a housing subsidy, such as a rental voucher, or because of the requirements of that assistance program.
rules.requirement_es: Los propietarios en Massachusetts no pueden discriminar a un inquilino porque recibe asistencia pública o un subsidio de vivienda, como un vale de alquiler, ni por los requisitos de ese programa de asistencia.

rules.title: Massachusetts security deposit limit and protections
rules.requirement: In Massachusetts, a security deposit cannot be more than one month's rent. The landlord must give receipts, keep it in a separate interest-bearing bank account in Massachusetts, pay you interest, and return it within 30 days after you move out, minus only allowed deductions.

El propietario debe darle recibos, guardarlo en una cuenta bancaria separada con intereses en Massachusetts, pagarle intereses y devolverlo dentro de 30 días después de que usted se mude, menos solo las deducciones permitidas.

rules.title: Rental application fee cap
rules.requirement: A landlord or agent cannot charge more than $50 for a rental application fee. The cap goes up each year with inflation.
rules.requirement_es: Un propietario o su agente no puede cobrar más de $50 por la solicitud de alquiler. El límite se ajusta cada año según la inflación.

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act good-cause requirement
rules.requirement: A landlord can only evict a tenant or refuse to renew a lease (written or oral) for one of the good causes listed in state law, and must prove the cause in court. Except for unpaid rent, the landlord must give the tenant a written Notice to Quit describing the cause.
rules.requirement_es: El arrendador solo puede desalojar a un inquilino o negarse a renovar un contrato (escrito u oral) por una de las causas justificadas que indica la ley estatal, y debe probar la causa ante el tribunal. rules.requirement: Landlords cannot refuse to rent to you or treat you differently because of your source of lawful income (such as housing vouchers or benefits), or because of race, religion, disability, familial status, and other protected traits.
rules.requirement_es: Los arrendadores no pueden negarse a alquilarle ni tratarle de manera diferente por la fuente de sus ingresos legales (como vales de vivienda o beneficios), ni por raza, religión, discapacidad, situación familiar y otras características protegidas.

rules.requirement: A landlord cannot collect a security deposit of more than one and a half times one month's rent. Any yearly increase in the deposit cannot be more than 10% of the current deposit, and the deposit must be returned with interest, minus allowed deductions, within 30 days after the tenancy ends.
rules.requirement_es: El arrendador no puede cobrar un depósito de seguridad de más de una vez y media el alquiler de un mes. Cualquier aumento anual del depósito no puede superar el 10% del depósito actual, y el depósito debe devolverse con intereses, menos las deducciones permitidas, dentro de los 30 días después de que termine el arrendamiento.
rules.coverage_text: Applies to most residential rental properties, including mobile homes. Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings are exempt unless the tenant sends a written request to have the law apply (effective 30 days after the request).
